about: The sound whitelist: every sound a storyboard may name, with what it really sounds like. Hand-edited (make-catalog.mjs copies family/says/scenes into catalog.json). Written from engine/sfx/measure.mjs numbers and the source files, not by ear: Claude can't hear, Jonny's ears decide. A sound that isn't here can't be used, a sound with 'scenes' plays only in a clip that declares one of them ("sound": { "scenes": ["scifi"] }), and 'words' are the names Jonny uses (splort, dö-döm, bonk) that a storyboard may write instead of the id. 'same' = the raw family behind a named sound (use the named one). 'pending' = the sound arrives with an open branch. Search: node engine/sfx/whitelist.mjs wet

families.steps: footsteps, one take per footfall (the auto foley picks the floor from the set)
families.handling: hands and props: grabs, cloth, setting things down, sitting
families.hit: punches, thuds, knocks on wood, metal, glass and plates
families.body: breaths, gasps, heartbeats, mouth sounds, farts
families.cartoon: the engine's cartoon moves: hops, landings, pops, poofs, whooshes, little pings
families.signature: the three leads' fixed signature sounds
families.music: musical stings: a chord, a sad trombone, short jingles
families.street: horns, brakes, air doors, engines, lift doors
families.ui: screen sounds: menu beeps, clicks, swipes, glitches (only in a sci-fi clip or one with a screen)
families.scifi: synth blips, lasers, spaceship engines, sci-fi doors (only in a sci-fi clip or one with a screen)

scenes.ui: a phone, computer or lift panel on screen whose beeps and swipes we hear
scenes.jingle: the clip plays a musical game-show or video-game sting on purpose

hop.says: a quick little rising blip, 0.13 s (a cartoon jump)

land.says: a short low thump that drops in pitch (feet landing)

whoosh.says: air rushing past: a band of noise that swells and fades, about 0.3 s

charge.says: a rising electric whine with sparkles getting denser, 1.3 s (a spell charging up), sometimes a little chime on top

impact.says: a big deep boom that drops in pitch, with a metallic ring on top (a heavy cartoon hit)

poof.says: a soft puff of air going darker, about 0.9 s (a cloud of smoke); about half the time a little magic chime on top

pop.says: a bubble pop: a quick upward blip and a short ringing tone at 1.4 kHz

click.says: two tiny sharp clicks (a camera shutter or a light switch)

creak.says: a slow rough squeak wobbling around 650 Hz (a lid straining, a hinge)

shing.says: a bright metal ring that rises a little (a blade drawn, a sword gleam)

knock-tap.says: one hollow knuckle-on-door thud with a click on top (the engine's own knock; 'knock' is the AI one Jonny picked)

slam.says: a deep door thump, the frame rattling and a latch click (code-made)

tink.says: a tiny high metal ping, 0.35 s (a coin, a hat brim tapping something)

ting.says: a high bright bell ping that rings out, 0.7 s (light glinting off a blade): this is a 'bling'

crinkle.says: a few quick crisp crackles (a sweet wrapper)

latch.says: an iron latch dropping into its catch: a metal clack with a short ring (code-made)

papercut.says: a dry tearing hiss with a soft thock (a blade through paper or card)

gasp.says: a quick breathy inhale that rises (a small surprised gasp)

step.says: one heavy footstep on stone: a dull low thud and a little grit (code-made)

sting.says: one dark minor chord of buzzy saw tones, 0.7 s: a single 'dun!' (a shock). Off by default on a shocked face: "sound": { "autoSting": true }

screech.says: a narrow hissing squeal sliding down (brakes)

ring.says: an alarm clock: a hammer trilling fast between two high bells

scribble.says: a pencil writing fast: short scratchy strokes

bell.says: a school bell: a fast hammer on one big bell, about 1 s

splash.says: a puddle splash: a burst of noise and two falling bloops, 0.5 s

ding.says: one soft bell tone at 1.2 kHz that rings out for 1.6 s (a lift arriving)

doorslide.says: sliding doors gliding: a soft low rumble and a whisper of air (lift doors, automatic shop doors)

hiss.says: a short bright hiss of air (bus doors, air brakes)

partyhorn.says: a buzzy paper party horn that bends up as it unrolls

ringtone.says: a phone ringing: a fast trill of two tones in short bursts

flutter.says: a flurry of paper: many soft flaps thinning out

scrape.says: wooden stool feet dragged over a wooden floor: a woody, chattering rub

wings.says: soft feathery wing beats three times a second, for a hover (a bed; the auto wing flaps replace it where they play)

notify.says: a soft phone notification: two quick rounded tones going up a fourth

gunshot.says: a cartoon pistol: a sharp crack and a short low boom

sadslide.says: the sad trombone: four notes sliding down, 'wah wah wah-wahhh', 1.8 s. Off by default on a droop: "sound": { "autoTrombone": true }

puncture.says: a tiny dry card pop with a soft thock (a fang or straw through a carton), from its code

squirt.says: a wet, hissy jet whose pitch drops as the pressure goes, with bubbly flutter (a squeezed carton), from its code

splort.says: a soft wet slap, a squelch sinking in pitch, then a few drips (juice landing on a face), from its code

sig-phoenix.says: Phoenix's flame whoosh: air rushing in, a low 'fwoomp' and roar, embers crackling, a short bird cry, 1.3 s

sig-reaper.says: Reaper's bell: one deep church-bell toll in D that slowly swells and fades, 2.8 s

sig-wizard.says: the Wizard's sparkle: eight quick bell-like notes running up, a high twinkle and glitter, 1.4 s (heard as a 'bling')
